issues.title: Helper methods marked public inappropriately
issues.description: Helper methods checkUrl(), copyUrl(), and checkCopiedUrl() are marked public but are only used internally within the ClipBoardTests class. They should be marked private to minimize exposure of internal implementation details.

issues.title: Missing clipboard verification after copy operation
issues.description: The testClipboard() method copies the URL but skips the checkCopiedUrl() verification step that validates the clipboard contents match the expected URL. This test previously verified that the copied URL in the clipboard matches the browser's URL bar value, ensuring the copy operation worked correctly. Without this check, the test cannot detect if the copy operation failed or if the clipboard contains incorrect data, allowing clipboard-related bugs to pass undetected.

        checkUrl()
        copyUrl()

issues.title: Incorrect UI element verification for light theme selection
issues.description: After selecting light theme mode via Action.SelectLightTheme, the test verifies the wrong UI element by checking darkThemeView instead of lightThemeView. This causes the test to validate dark theme selection state when it should be verifying light theme was properly selected. The bug means the test will fail when light theme is correctly selected (darkThemeView will be '0' not '1'), or pass incorrectly if light theme selection fails but dark theme happens to be selected.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Select Light mode
        navigator.performAction(Action.SelectLightTheme)
        let lightIsSelected = app.buttons[AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.darkThemeView].value
        XCTAssertEqual(lightIsSelected as? String, "1")

issues.title: Navigation timing issue in settings toggle verification
issues.description: The test taps the 'Done' button before navigating to NewTabScreen, reversing the correct order of operations. The navigator.goto(NewTabScreen) call expects to transition from the settings screen, but 'Done' has already been tapped which dismisses the settings UI. This creates a race condition where the navigation command may fail or behave unpredictably because it's operating on an already-dismissed screen. The correct flow should be navigate first, then tap Done to confirm the navigation completed.

issues.title: Public methods lack required documentation comments
issues.description: The helper methods checkUrl(), copyUrl(), and checkCopiedUrl() were changed from internal to public visibility in this PR. According to AGENTS.md Rule 14, all public API elements must include triple-slash (///) documentation comments describing their purpose, behavior, parameters, and return values. These methods only have single-line comments (// Comment) instead of proper documentation comments (/// Comment). This violates the repository's explicit compliance rules for public APIs.

issues.title: Public helper methods lack required documentation comments
issues.description: The helper methods `checkUrl()`, `copyUrl()`, and `checkCopiedUrl()` were changed to `public` but do not have triple-slash (`///`) documentation comments as required for public APIs.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31612 - [MTE-5149] - delete auto tests

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes obsolete XCUI tests and their test-plan entries: `testCopyLink` in ClipBoardTests, and `testSetCustomURLAsHome` in HomePageSettingsUITests (which was already permanently skipped via `XCTSkipIf(true)`). The `testCopyLink` body was entirely commented out apart from opening a URL, so it asserted nothing and removing it is safe. The test-plan JSON files still parse and the removed names are dropped consistently across AccessibilityTestPlan, Smoketest, TAESmokeTestPlan and FullFunctionalTestPlan.

The rest of the PR is less safe. The `testCheckSystemThemeChanges` edit changes the light-theme assertion to read the dark-theme button, so that assertion can no longer pass. The `checkCopiedUrl()` call is removed from `testClipboard` without replacement, which weakens that test, and the helpers gain unneeded `public` modifiers. The `Done`/`goto(NewTabScreen)` order is also swapped in `testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection` with no explanation. The PR description says a new test case was created, but the diff edits the existing test in place.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The deletions are fine, but the edit to testCheckSystemThemeChanges introduces a guaranteed assertion failure. The removed verification in testClipboard and the unexplained navigation reorder are also regressions in test coverage and behaviour that the author should justify or revert.

architecture.overview:
The XCUITest suite is driven by `.xctestplan` files that list each test or test class to run. Each UI test class extends `BaseTestCase`, uses the `navigator` helper to move between screens, and locates elements through `AccessibilityIdentifiers`. This PR touches only test code and test plans: it removes entries from four plans and deletes or edits three test methods. It does not touch the app code under test.

The main risk is in test logic rather than configuration. The theme test now reads the dark-theme button when it should read the light-theme button, and the clipboard test no longer checks the copied URL. Both changes make the suites less accurate, even though the plan edits themselves are consistent.
steps: Start at the test plans (AccessibilityTestPlan, Smoketest, TAESmokeTestPlan, FullFunctionalTestPlan). Each lists test identifiers, and this PR removes `ClipBoardTests/testCopyLink()` and `HomePageSettingsUITests/testSetCustomURLAsHome()` from them.

In ClipBoardTests, `testCopyLink` is deleted. Its body was commented out apart from opening a URL. The `testClipboard` flow loses its `checkCopiedUrl()` call, which leaves that helper unused, and the helpers gain `public` modifiers.
In HomePageSettingsUITests, the permanently skipped `testSetCustomURLAsHome` is deleted. In `testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection`, the `Done` tap now runs before `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)`.

In DisplaySettingsTests, `testCheckSystemThemeChanges` is edited in place and its TestRail link is updated. The light-theme check now reads `darkThemeView`, which is the wrong button for that assertion.

findings.title: Light-theme assertion reads the dark-theme button
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/DisplaySettingsTests.swift`, `testCheckSystemThemeChanges` (around line 53) reads `AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.darkThemeView` for the light-theme assertion. Change that read back to `lightThemeView` so the value checked after `SelectLightTheme` is the light button. Keep the variable name `lightIsSelected` consistent with what it reads. Also reconcile the PR description, which claims a new test case was added, with the in-place edit and the changed TestRail ID (2337487 → 3298823). Confirm the intended test mapping.

findings.title: Clipboard test no longer verifies the copied URL
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ClipBoardTests.swift`, `testClipboard` (around lines 66-73) previously called `checkCopiedUrl()` right after `copyUrl()`, and this PR removed that call. Restore it unless there is a documented reason for removal. If the check is unreliable, keep the call and gate it on the existing `#unavailable(iOS 16.0)` condition rather than deleting it. Leave `checkCopiedUrl` in place only if it is still called; otherwise remove the dead helper.

findings.title: Unexplained reorder of Done and navigator.goto in disable-top-sites test
findings.body:
In `testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection`, the `Done` button is now tapped before `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)`, where the original order was the reverse. The PR description does not mention this change. `navigator.goto` relies on the app's current screen state, so changing the order could leave the navigator's expected screen out of sync with what is on screen. Tapping `Done` from the Shortcuts settings page only makes sense if that page is still the active screen, which I did not confirm. Either the reorder fixes a real timing issue that should be explained in the PR, or it is an accidental edit.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/HomePageSettingsUITest.swift" lines="152-158"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/HomePageSettingsUITest.swift`, `testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection` (around lines 155-156) now taps `app.buttons["Done"]` before `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)`. The original order was the reverse. Check how `navigator.goto` tracks the current screen and whether the Shortcuts settings page is still active when `Done` is tapped. Restore the original order unless the reorder is needed to fix a real issue, in which case explain it in a comment.

findings.title: Public modifiers added to test helpers without need
findings.body:
`checkUrl`, `copyUrl` and `checkCopiedUrl` are now marked `public` inside an internal `XCTestCase` subclass. Nothing outside the test target uses them, and the rest of the XCUITests suite does not mark its helpers `public`. The change adds noise with no benefit.

::diff{file="firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ClipBoardTests.swift" lines="10-19"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/firefox-ios-tests/Tests/XCUITests/ClipBoardTests.swift`, remove the `public` modifier from `checkUrl()`, `copyUrl()` and `checkCopiedUrl()` (around lines 11, 17 and 41). Match the other XCUITests helpers, which are plain `func` declarations with no access modifier.

findings.title: Deleted tests were correct to remove, and test plans stay consistent
findings.body:
`testCopyLink` was an empty shell. Apart from `navigator.openURL` and `waitForTabsButton`, its body was commented out, so it asserted nothing. `testSetCustomURLAsHome` was disabled by an unconditional `XCTSkipIf(true)`. Removing both is a good cleanup. The matching entries are removed from all four `.xctestplan` files, and I checked that each plan still parses as valid JSON.

The skip referenced issue #28117, so that link to the open bug is now gone from the codebase. The issue itself is unaffected.
